readme_snippet: Code Audit — dual parallel agent review (Opus + Codex) Two independent deep agent-audits run in PARALLEL on the same change — an adversarial Opus agent and a Codex agent (codex exec) — then their findings are merged/deduped and fixed, iterating up to 3 rounds (fix → re-audit the corrected state) until a round is clean. Why parallel, not Opus-then-Codex. Different models catch different things — the union is the value (e.g. Opus reconciles SQL to the dollar; Codex catches a non-executable cron wrapper). They run on separate backends (Anthropic + OpenAI) so there's zero mutual contention, and both are non-blocking. Duplicate findings are cheap — the merge dedups them, and a finding flagged by both is just higher confidence. The one thing parallel loses — Codex never seeing the fixes — is recovered by re-auditing the corrected state each round (the loop below).

It triggers iterative planning with Planner, Architect, and Critic agents until consensus is reached, with RALPLAN-DR structured deliberation (short mode by default, deliberate mode for high-risk work). Flags --interactive: Enables user prompts at key decision points (draft review in step 2 and final approval in step 6). Without this flag the workflow runs fully automated — Planner → Architect → Critic loop — marks the final plan pending approval, outputs it, and stops without asking for confirmation or executing changes. --deliberate: Forces deliberate mode for high-risk work. Adds pre-mortem (3 scenarios) and expanded test planning (unit/integration/e2e/observability). Without this flag, deliberate mode can still auto-enable when the request explicitly signals high risk (auth/security, migrations, destructive changes, production incidents, compliance/PII, public API breakage).
